title: Treatment of the anterior cruciate ligament rupture with a magnesium-based interference screw: a single group multicenter trial
summary:
The CE-certified bioresorbable and magnesium-based interference screw MAGNEZIX® IFSc for the treatment of injuries of the anterior cruciate ligament is to be investigated. 
The treatment consists of a surgical stabilization by a so-called ACL replacement plastic. A conservative, i.e. non-surgical treatment is not an alternative.
The fixation of the tendon can be achieved by different techniques. A procedure that has been recognized for decades is the use of so-called interference screws. These are offered by different manufacturers, whereby resorbable (dissolving) and non-absorbable (non-dissolving) screws are offered. In the past 15 years, resorbable screws have been used almost exclusively. The main reasons are advantages in control examinations such as MRIs (magnetic resonance imaging) and the avoidance of necessary second operations.
In the present study, the magnesium-based interference screw (IFSc) from Syntellix AG (Hannover) is used. This screw has the advantage that it consists mainly of magnesium, has a strength comparable to natural bone and dissolves by itself over time and is replaced by the body with bone-like material. This means that this screw is biodegradable.
conditions: Rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL)

interventions.name: Replacement of the anterior cruciate ligament with the semitendinosus tendon in case of a new anterior cruciate ligament rupture. The tendon is fixated with a MAGNEZIX® IFSc interference screw.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Anterior cruciate ligament rupture leading to an at least 5mm side-to-side difference of antero-posterior translation in the Lachman Test of the knee, using a KT-1000.
2. Age ≥18 years.
3. Written informed consent for trial.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Multi ligament injury, such as concomitant collateral ligament and/or the posterior cruciate ligament injuries.
2. History of ligament injuries of the contralateral knee.
3. Primary or secondary osteoporosis.
4. Existing degeneration of the meniscus.
5. Degenerative cartilage damage in the sense of an emerging or manifest arthrosis which is latestly diagnosed intraoperatively during the arthroscopic staging.
6. Pregnancy, suspected pregnancy or breastfeeding period.
